spans.s:
Usra, m.; Usrā, f.; Usrika, m.; Usriya, m.; Usriyā, f. All these words denote a ‘bull’ or a ‘cow,’ occurring frequently in the Rigveda, and sometimes later, but usually with some reference to the morning light. In some passages the sense is doubtful. See Go.
Foot notes usra, Rv. vi. 12, 4; usrā, i. 3, 8; viii. 75, 8; 96, 8; ix. 58, 2, etc.; usrika, i. 190, 5; usriya, v. 58, 6 (with vṛṣabhaḥ); ix. 74. 3; usriyā, i. 153, 4; 180, 3; ii. 40, 2, etc. In ix. 70, 6, usriya is applied to a calf; and in ix. 68, 1; 93, 2, usriyā means ‘milk.’
Usrau dhūrṣāhau, Vājasaneyi Saṃhitā, iv. 33; usrā, Av. xii. 3, 37; usriya, Av. i. 12, 1; usriyā, Av. ix. 4, 1; Vājasaneyi Saṃhitā, xxxv. 2. 3. In Av. v. 20, 1; 28, 3, it means ‘cowhide,’ or perhaps in v. 28, 3, ‘milk.’
